source: Tan, Tamisha & Kühlert (2020), in the Proceedings of the Workshop on Turkic and Languages in Contact with Turkic 5. 140–154.
notes: Finally, passives and impersonals also differ in their behaviour in non-finite clauses. As in Turkish (16), the impersonal argument can both control and be controlled PRO.
en: One does not want PRO to die in war.

source: Tan, Tamisha & Kühlert (2020), in the Proceedings of the Workshop on Turkic and Languages in Contact with Turkic 5. 140–154.
notes: Finally, passives and impersonals also differ in their behaviour in non-finite clauses. As in Turkish (16), the impersonal argument can both control and be controlled PRO.
en: One loves PRO to arrive by car.

source: Tan, Tamisha & Kühlert (2020), in the Proceedings of the Workshop on Turkic and Languages in Contact with Turkic 5. 140–154.
notes: In contrast, the promoted theme of a matrix passive cannot control PRO.
en: I want the book to be read (*by me).

source: Tan, Tamisha & Kühlert (2020), in the Proceedings of the Workshop on Turkic and Languages in Contact with Turkic 5. 140–154.
notes: While (28) is fine with the reading that the speaker wants the book to be read by someone else/in general, it is wholly ungrammatical under the interpretation that the speaker wants to read the book themselves. One also cannot passivise both the matrix and embedded clause.
en: Intended: ‘I am wanted to be liked (by myself/someone else).’
